rulebook.rule: For mean‑reversion entries, require the price to touch a defined support (e.g., 20‑day SMA) and exhibit at least one bounce before taking the position.
Replace hard intraday time‑stops with a trailing stop when the trade’s expected R exceeds 0.2; only use a time‑stop if the expected R is ≤0.2.
Do not take long mean‑reversion trades on assets that are below both the 20‑day and 50‑day SMA unless a clear fundamental catalyst is present.
Do not enter short or fade trades on high-beta single stocks unless the price has confirmed a breakdown below its 20-day low.
For all mean-reversion long setups, require a confirmed higher-low candle close on the daily chart before entry rather than bidding directly into falling prices.

letters.title: Weekly Desk Update – 2026-10-18
letters.body:
Dear Erwann,

Our $10,000 paper account finished the week at $9,527.61, a 4.73% decline. By contrast the S&P 500 proxy fell only 0.72% (from 10,000 to 9,928). The gap tells us the desk under‑performed the market, largely because our tactical bucket generated a net loss of $412.50 across ten closed trades (30% win‑rate, avg R ‑0.35).

**Best trades** – The USD/JPY trend‑pullback long produced a modest $10.35 profit (R +0.15) and the RKLX mean‑reversion long gave $40.05 (R +0.27). Both succeeded because the price respected the 20‑day SMA before moving in our favour and we allowed enough room for the move to develop.

**Worst trades** – The DOGE/USD mean‑reversion long lost $91.09 (R ‑1.03) and the EUR/GBP long lost $162.88 (R ‑1.36). In each case we entered on an oversold signal while the asset was below multiple moving averages and fundamental pressure was strongly negative. The trade was stopped out quickly, confirming that the signal alone was insufficient.

**What worked** – Trend‑pullback entries that waited for a bounce off a key SMA and used a trailing stop captured small upside without being clipped by a hard time‑stop. The RKLX trade exemplifies this.

**What didn’t** – Over‑reliance on extreme oversold/overbought readings, especially on assets with weak fundamentals (FMC, EUR/GBP, DOGE). Tight intraday time‑stops also ate into winners (USD/JPY, USD/CHF) and forced premature exits on losers.

**Caution vs. looseness** – The engine skipped 49 ideas, many of which were short signals on crypto (DOGE, HYPE) that our long‑only crypto rule blocked. Those missed shorts would have been profitable, suggesting we are too restrictive on the short side. At the same time, our time‑stop discipline is too loose, cutting winners before they can realise their expected R.

**Plan for next week** – 1) Add a confirmation filter for mean‑reversion trades (price must test a support level and show a bounce). 2) Replace hard intraday time‑stops with dynamic trailing stops for any trade with expected R > 0.2. 3) Open a short‑crypto lane for high‑probability short ideas that meet our risk criteria. We will keep position sizing modest (max 2% of equity per trade) and monitor draw‑down closely.

Regards,
The AI Trading Desk

letters.title: Desk Letter: Week Ending October 25, 2026
letters.body:
Erwann,

This week was an unvarnished setback for the desk. Our paper account declined 8.89%, falling from $9,543.21 to $8,694.61. Over the same stretch, our S&P 500 benchmark dipped just 0.42% (from 9,928.07 to 9,886.32). Our heavy underperformance stemmed from aggressive counter-trend positioning and poor risk management on the short side.

Our best closed trade was a short on GBP/JPY, netting +$46.38 (+0.47 R). The thesis played out as forecast, but an arbitrary 1–5 day time stop closed the position prematurely, leaving significant profit on the table. Our worst trade was a short on SMCI, which cost us -$204.43 (-1.83 R). We attempted to fade momentum into earnings/catalyst optimism, and the stock triggered a violent short squeeze that overshot our intended stop-loss.

What worked: directional macro forecasts when aligned with technical structure. What failed completely: fighting strong trends across FX (USD/MXN short, EUR/CHF long) and catching falling knives in crypto (ADA and UNI longs both took full -1.0 R stops).

Regarding discipline, the desk was simultaneously too loose on trade entries and too timid on trade management. We took 14 closed setups across noisy instruments with an unacceptable 14% win rate this week. Yet on our two winning trades (GBP/JPY and IONQ), we clamped profits early with rigid calendar time stops rather than letting the thesis run. On the passing side, the engine properly filtered out multiple weak altcoins (DOT, ONDO, AAVE), which prevented further bleed.

Our historical backtests clearly confirm that shorting overbought conditions has negative expectancy across thousands of trials (-0.104 R average). For next week, we are eliminating unhedged equity shorts in high-beta momentum names, requiring verified reversal candle confirmation on all mean-reversion entries, and enforcing wider profit targets for winning positions.
